title: Global Semiconductor Equipment Billings Increased 23% Year-Over-Year in Q2 2026, SEMI Reports
gist: SEMI's WWSEMS report shows global semiconductor equipment billings hit a record $40.53bn in Q2 2026, up 23% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter -- the second consecutive record quarter -- with the industry association attributing the acceleration to AI infrastructure investment across Asia, North America and Europe.

insights.claim: Global semiconductor equipment billings reached $40.53bn in the second quarter of 2026, up 23% year-over-year and 11% quarter-over-quarter, according to SEMI's Worldwide Semiconductor Equipment Market Statistics (WWSEMS) report.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: A 23% YoY, 11% QoQ acceleration in equipment billings is a hard, industry-wide confirmation of accelerating fab capex, useful as a coincident cross-check against individual equipment makers' own guidance.
insights.quote: global semiconductor equipment billings increased 23% year-over-year to US$40.53 billion in the second quarter of 2026

insights.claim: Q2 2026 marks the second consecutive record quarter for global semiconductor equipment billings.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Back-to-back records indicate the current equipment upcycle is sustained momentum rather than a single-quarter spike, supporting continued near-term capex from chipmakers and their suppliers.
insights.quote: The results mark a second consecutive record quarter
insights.locator: The results mark a second consecutive record quarter

insights.claim: SEMI President and CEO Ajit Manocha attributed the record billings to the industry's sustained investment in advanced manufacturing capacity needed to support rising chip demand, particularly for AI infrastructure, with growth registered across Asia, North America and Europe.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: Broad-based regional growth (not concentrated in one geography) suggests AI-driven equipment demand is a global phenomenon rather than a single country's stimulus or reshoring effect.
insights.quote: Growth across Asia, North America and Europe underscores the global nature of this demand and the critical role of semiconductor manufacturing in enabling the next wave of AI-driven innovation.
insights.locator: said Ajit Manocha, SEMI President and CEO

themes.theme: Scope and provenance of the data

insights.claim: The WWSEMS report is compiled from monthly billings data submitted by members of SEMI and the Semiconductor Equipment Association of Japan (SEAJ), covering seven regions and more than 22 market segments.
insights.speaker: SemiWiki
insights.so_what: The breadth of segment and regional coverage makes this a useful macro cross-check on the semiconductor capital-equipment cycle, though it is self-reported by member companies and industry-association-framed rather than independently audited.
